meta.title: PlanVisAR model and pipeline visualization data
meta.note: Every number in charts[] is copied from a repo output file named in that chart's 'source', except where 'source' says it was computed by running repo code (no code was changed). Kaggle runs v3-v8 use CubiCasa5k sample 6044 (high_quality_architectural); v9 and local/ use sample 10052 (colorful). The two samples are not directly comparable.

nodes.label: Floorplan image
nodes.desc: PNG/JPG of a 2D plan, any resolution. Sample: CubiCasa5k colorful/10052/F1_original.png (geometry-v2 cell 4).

nodes.label: Preprocess + auto-crop
nodes.desc: Resize to 512x512, ImageNet mean/std normalization. Pass 1 on whole sheet; if prob>0.3 bbox +8% margin covers <50% of sheet, re-infer on the crop (geometry-v2 cell 4).

nodes.label: MitUNet wall segmentation
nodes.desc: MiT-b4 Mix-Transformer encoder + U-Net decoder with scSE attention, 1 output class (wall). Weights: MitUNet_cubicasa-5k_a62_mit_b4_tversky_7666_30E.pth, 257.4 MB (geometry-v2 cells 2-3).

nodes.label: CubiCasa multi-task net
nodes.desc: hg_furukawa_original hourglass network, 44 output channels = 21 junction heatmaps + 12 room classes + 11 icon classes. Gives second-opinion rooms, walls, doors and windows (planliftar_cubicasa cells 0-6).

nodes.label: Wall probability map
nodes.desc: Sigmoid output resized back to original size with bilinear interpolation, kept as float [0,1] and cached as wall_prob_crop.npy (geometry-v2 cell 4).

nodes.label: Hysteresis healing
nodes.desc: Strong wall >=0.50, weak wall >=0.25 kept only if connected to strong. Heals confidence dips (geometry-v2 cell 5).

nodes.label: Wall thickness + micro-gap seal
nodes.desc: t_med = 2 x median distance-transform value on the skeleton. Morphological CLOSE with a (1.5 x t_med) square kernel seals hairline breaks while leaving door-size gaps alone (geometry-v2 cell 6).

nodes.label: Virtual door/window seals
nodes.desc: Labeling copy only: mask OR rasterized CubiCasa walls, plus bars 1.6 x opening width across each CubiCasa door/window. Never exported (geometry-v2 cell 7).

nodes.label: Rooms-first region extraction
nodes.desc: 4-connected components of the non-wall space. Border-touching = exterior; others >= MIN_ROOM_AREA are rooms. Contours simplified with approxPolyDP(eps = 1% perimeter). Closed by construction (geometry-v2 cell 8).

nodes.label: Nearest-label wall derivation
nodes.desc: Every wall pixel assigned to nearest room label via Euclidean distance transform; borders between two labels become wall runs with thickness read from the distance transform (geometry-v2 cell 8; local post-process consensus_lab.py:933).

nodes.label: Consensus check vs CubiCasa
nodes.desc: IoU matrix MitUNet rooms x CubiCasa rooms, Hungarian 1:1 match at IoU>=0.5 (legacy) or area-weighted graded score (local). Advisory: agreement is evidence, not a verdict (geometry-v2 cells 9-10; consensus_lab.py:368, :1143).

nodes.label: Watershed virtual split
nodes.desc: Only for scoring merged regions: seeds at CubiCasa room centroids, watershed on -distance transform. Never adds exported walls (geometry-v2 cell 11).

nodes.label: Invariants
nodes.desc: All polygons closed, every room >= MIN_ROOM_AREA, 1-40 rooms, at least one room; loose wall endpoints = warning only (geometry-v2 cell 10).

nodes.label: Acceptance barrier
nodes.desc: Single exit. Rejected plans write no geometry, only acceptance_report.json with machine-readable reject_reasons (geometry-v2 cell 12).

nodes.label: JSON export (doors carved)
nodes.desc: schema 2.0: walls (px), rooms (polygons), fixtures, scale {units: relative_px, user_scale_required: true}. Door spans cut out of wall runs (geometry-v2 cell 13).

nodes.label: Gap closure (plan_ops)
nodes.desc: Normalize schema, weld dangling endpoints within 3 x t_med; longer spans only if a window lies on the line; never across a door (deliverables/plan_ops.py:144; JS port livemap/plan_ops.js:171).

nodes.label: 3D extrusion (GLB)
nodes.desc: One box per wall (length x thickness x 2.5 m height) + 0.02 m floor slab, recentered on footprint, plan (x,y) -> world (x,-y) (deliverables/glb_builder.py:59).

nodes.label: AR placement + scale
nodes.desc: WebXR/ARCore hit-test on a tracked surface, anchor at tap, ppm = longest plan side px / user-typed metres, optional 1:N miniature scale (livemap/ar.html:641, :848, :1885).

blocks.label: Input
blocks.detail: RGB, resized to 512x512, ImageNet normalization mean (0.485,0.456,0.406) std (0.229,0.224,0.225)

blocks.label: MiT-b4 stage 1
blocks.detail: Overlapping patch embed 7x7 stride 4; efficient self-attention (reduction ratio 8) + Mix-FFN; 3 blocks

blocks.label: MiT-b4 stage 2
blocks.detail: Patch merge 3x3 stride 2; reduction ratio 4; 8 blocks

blocks.label: MiT-b4 stage 3
blocks.detail: Patch merge 3x3 stride 2; reduction ratio 2; 27 blocks

blocks.label: MiT-b4 stage 4 (bottleneck)
blocks.detail: Patch merge 3x3 stride 2; full attention; 3 blocks

blocks.label: U-Net decoder block 1 + scSE
blocks.detail: Upsample x2, concat skip, scSE, 2x(3x3 conv-BN-ReLU), scSE

blocks.label: Decoder blocks 4-5
blocks.detail: MiT has no 1/2-scale feature; smp feeds an empty skip there, so these blocks only upsample + convolve

blocks.label: Segmentation head
blocks.detail: 3x3 conv to 1 channel; sigmoid applied in notebook

blocks.label: Input
blocks.detail: RGB at native resolution, scaled to [-1,1] (2*x-1)

blocks.label: Stem
blocks.detail: 7x7 stride-2 conv 3->64, BN, ReLU, 2x2 max-pool, residual blocks to 256 ch

blocks.label: Hourglass encoder
blocks.detail: Four more 2x2 max-pools down to 1/64; residual blocks at 256 ch (512 at deepest); parallel skip branches at each scale

blocks.label: Hourglass decoder
blocks.detail: Four 512-ch transposed-conv x2 stages, each added to its skip branch, back to 1/4

blocks.label: 1x1 conv head + x4 upsample
blocks.detail: 1x1 convs 512->512->256->44, transposed conv k4 s4 back to input size

blocks.label: 21 junction heatmaps
blocks.detail: Sigmoid; wall/opening/icon corner junctions used by get_polygons() to build wall rectangles

blocks.label: 12 room classes
blocks.detail: Background, Outdoor, Wall, Kitchen, Living Room, Bed Room, Bath, Entry, Railing, Storage, Garage, Undefined

blocks.label: 11 icon classes
blocks.detail: Includes Window (class 1) and Door (class 2), which PlanVisAR uses as fixtures

models.name: MitUNet
models.role: Primary wall segmenter; its probability map is the geometry source
models.encoder: MiT-b4 (SegFormer Mix-Transformer), transplanted from smp.Segformer into smp.Unet
models.attention: scSE (concurrent spatial + channel squeeze-and-excitation) in every decoder block
models.training_data: CubiCasa5k (this checkpoint); upstream also publishes a regional fine-tune
models.license: Code MIT; weights CC BY-NC 4.0 (inherited from CubiCasa5k)

models.name: CubiCasa multi-task net
models.role: Second opinion: rooms, wall polygons, doors, windows

charts.title: Rooms found per Kaggle run
charts.caption: v3/v4 found 0 rooms on full-sheet plan 6044: the plan filled only part of the 512x512 input. Auto-crop (v5+) and CubiCasa seal hints recovered 5 closed rooms. v9 is a different plan (10052).
charts.source: v3_stdout.txt, v4_stdout.txt, v5_stdout.txt, v6_out.txt, v7_out.txt, v8_out.txt, v9_out.txt

charts.title: Consensus score per Kaggle run
charts.caption: v6 to v8 rose because of better CubiCasa room filtering (29 -> 28 -> 10 rooms counted), not because the walls changed. The 0.70 target was never reached; calibration was deferred (planliftar-v1-execution.md, Phase 2 gate).

charts.title: Wall-mask fragments through the healing stages
charts.caption: Ideal is 1. Hysteresis did not merge any fragments on these samples; the thickness-relative CLOSE removed one. Honest result: the healing layers matter less than the seal hints on these plans.

charts.title: Measured median wall thickness (t_med)
charts.caption: All tolerances are expressed as multiples of t_med, so they adapt to each image. Kernel = int(1.5 x t_med) | 1.

charts.title: Wall run clean-up funnel (local harness)
charts.caption: Region-border tracing emits every wall roughly twice; post-processing cuts 240 runs to 73 with all tolerances in t_med units.

charts.title: Per-room agreement with CubiCasa (graded consensus)
charts.caption: Area-weighted mean = 0.343 vs legacy Hungarian score 0.077. Only the bedroom clears the legacy 0.5 cutoff; the kitchen misses it by 0.052.

charts.title: Same plan, three consensus measurements
charts.caption: The legacy metric gives zero credit below IoU 0.5 and counts the larger room list as denominator; graded consensus gives partial credit and treats open-plan merges as agreement.

charts.title: Resolution invariance test (normalised to 1x)
charts.caption: Same plan run at half, native and double resolution: identical room count, wall length within 1.0%, room area within 1.1%. All metrics PASS.

charts.title: Graded consensus vs true overlap (property test)
charts.caption: Synthetic test: score rises steadily with overlap, with no jump at the 50% majority-ownership gate. 25-way over-segmentation scores 0.04, a clean open-plan merge scores 1.0.

charts.title: Wall-gap closure on the bundled plans
charts.caption: Rooms-first output needs 4 connectors over 244 walls; the old line-first output needs 6 over 9 walls. Closure only fills gaps with evidence.
charts.source: Computed 2026-11-20 by running deliverables/plan_ops.py prepare_plan() unmodified on deliverables/livemap/plans/*.json

charts.title: Extruded 3D model size
charts.caption: Placeholder scale 100 px/m; real scale comes from the user in AR. Each wall is one 8-vertex, 12-triangle box, plus one floor slab (976 = 122 x 8; 1464 = 122 x 12).

charts.title: MitUNet published accuracy (upstream, regional dataset)
charts.caption: Reported by the MitUNet authors for their fine-tuned model on their regional dataset, not measured in this repo. The repo uses the CubiCasa5k-trained checkpoint.

glossary.def: Labelling every pixel of an image with a class. Here: wall or not-wall.
An image the same size as the plan where each pixel holds the model's confidence (0 to 1) that it is wall.
The encoder shrinks the image into compact features that describe what is where; the decoder grows them back to full size to draw the mask.
An encoder-decoder network whose decoder reuses fine detail from the encoder through skip connections. Standard for precise masks.
A layer that lets every image patch look at every other patch, so the model sees the whole plan's layout at once, not just a small neighbourhood.
The SegFormer encoder: a four-stage transformer that outputs features at 1/4, 1/8, 1/16 and 1/32 of the image size. b4 is the second-largest size.
Concurrent spatial and channel squeeze-and-excitation: small gates that boost useful feature channels and image locations and damp background noise.
A training loss that weighs missed wall pixels and false wall pixels differently (alpha 0.6 / beta 0.4), to favour thin, complete walls.
One network that predicts several things at once. CubiCasa's predicts wall junctions, room types and icons (doors, windows, fixtures) from one image.
A per-pixel score for 'a wall corner or T-junction of this type is here'. CubiCasa joins junctions into wall rectangles.
Two thresholds: pixels above the high one are wall; pixels above the low one count only if they touch confirmed wall. Heals faint breaks without adding noise.
For each wall pixel, the distance to the nearest non-wall pixel. Twice that value on the centreline is the wall's thickness.
Thinning a shape to a one-pixel centreline. Used to sample wall thickness on the centre of each wall.
Median wall thickness in pixels for this image. Every tolerance in the pipeline is a multiple of it, so results do not depend on image resolution.
Grow then shrink a mask. Gaps narrower than the kernel close; wider gaps such as doorways survive.
Groups of touching pixels. Applied to the empty space between walls, each group is a room or the outside.
Find the enclosed spaces first, then derive walls from their borders. Rooms are closed by construction, so the 3D model has no accidental holes.
Classic line detector. The original prototype used it; it produced disconnected segments, which is why the project moved to rooms-first.
OpenCV's Douglas-Peucker simplification: turns a jagged pixel outline into a polygon with few corners.
Overlap of two shapes divided by their combined area. 1 = identical, 0 = no overlap.
Finds the best one-to-one pairing between two lists (MitUNet rooms and CubiCasa rooms) maximising total IoU.
How well the two independent models agree on the rooms. Evidence of correctness, never ground truth.
Floods a shape from seed points; where floods meet is a dividing line. Used only to score whether a merged region splits into the rooms CubiCasa sees.
Rules every accepted plan must satisfy regardless of any model: closed polygons, minimum room area, sane room count.
The single decision point. Fail and the plan is rejected with machine-readable reasons; no 3D file is produced.
The standard binary 3D model file format for the web and AR viewers.
Turning a 2D line into a 3D box by giving it thickness and height.
WebXR is the browser AR standard; ARCore is Google's Android AR engine underneath it that tracks the phone and finds surfaces.
Casting a ray from the screen centre to find where it meets a detected real surface. Where the placement ring appears.
A point tied to a real-world spot that ARCore keeps updated as its map improves, so the model stays put.
Scale factor. The user types the building's longest real side; ppm = longest plan side in pixels / metres.
Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial. Free for research and teaching; not for commercial products. Applies to CubiCasa5k and every model trained on it.

faq.q: Is this 'AI'? What exactly did you train?
faq.a: We did not train a model. We use two published, pretrained neural networks (MitUNet and the CubiCasa5k multi-task network) and contribute the pipeline around them: probability-map healing, rooms-first geometry, two-model consensus, an acceptance barrier and the AR client.
Each one makes mistakes. Where two independent models agree on a room, that is evidence it is right; where they disagree, the plan is flagged. Neither is treated as the answer key.

faq.q: Why MitUNet for walls instead of CubiCasa's own walls?
faq.a: MitUNet is a newer wall-specialist (transformer encoder + U-Net + attention) designed for thin structures. CubiCasa's walls are used only as sealing hints and its rooms only for scoring.

faq.q: Your consensus is 0.07-0.34, below the 0.70 target. Does the pipeline fail?
faq.a: The legacy score is pulled down by measurement artefacts we documented: margin regions counted as rooms, CubiCasa's own fragment rooms, and a hard 0.5 cutoff (the kitchen scored 0.448). The graded metric reports 0.343 on the same plan. The 0.70 threshold is deliberately uncalibrated until multi-sample validation, and consensus is advisory; hard invariants decide acceptance.

faq.q: How do you get real-world size from an image?
faq.a: We do not guess it. The export is unitless (relative_px). In AR the user types one real dimension (the building's longest side) and every wall scales from that.

faq.q: Does it work on images of different resolutions?
faq.a: Yes. All thresholds are multiples of measured wall thickness. Our resolution test at 0.5x, 1x and 2x gave the same 13 rooms and wall length within 1%.

faq.q: What happens with open-plan living/dining areas?
faq.a: They come out as one room. The pipeline never invents a wall in open space; it notes 'merged_rooms' and accepts the plan if invariants pass.

faq.q: Can a bad plan produce a broken 3D model?
faq.a: The acceptance barrier is the only exit. A plan that fails invariants is rejected with reasons such as open_polygon or room_below_min_area, and no geometry file is written.
Yes. Door spans are carved out of exported wall runs, and gap closure refuses to fill any gap a door sits on.

Not with the current weights. Both models are trained on CubiCasa5k, licensed CC BY-NC 4.0. A commercial launch needs retraining on owned or permissively licensed data; the pipeline code itself is unaffected.

faq.q: Why does it need a GPU?
faq.a: Only the two neural-network forward passes. Everything after the probability map is CPU image processing, which is why the local harness runs on a laptop from a cached map.

Its authors report 87.91% mIoU and 85.01% boundary IoU on their regional dataset. We have not measured pixel accuracy on our own data; our evaluation is geometric (closed rooms, consensus, resolution invariance).

Page-margin regions that do not touch the border can be counted as rooms (now gated by a wall-ink test), the CLOSE seal can weld narrow corridors (instrumented, not yet seen), derived walls can be slightly off-axis, and a single-point centroid filter can drop large rooms.
